correctness.rationale: The source H-description is reconstructed with the correct affine hyperplane and all nonempty proper subset facets. Inclusion-exclusion gives the exact run-length formula for every facet height. The merge identity for Phi proves the sharp lower bound f_n(X)>=n|X|(n-|X|)/2 and shows equality exactly for prefixes/suffixes. Intrinsic normal lengths then give the centered facet-distance minimum at the four endpoint facets. Opposite endpoint facets give a matching upper bound for every possible center, and their equality constraints together with strict slack of all other facets prove the incenter-set dimension n-3.

value.rationale: Strong rectangulotopes are a new explicit quotientope family whose skeleta encode flip graphs of strong rectangulations and cease to be combinatorially permutahedral beyond n=4. The theorem identifies a family-wide metric invariant and a sharp containment by an n-scaled centered permutahedron. The equality classification explains exactly which facets retain permutahedral tightness, while the incenter-dimension formula exposes a nontrivial positive-dimensional optimal-center phenomenon. This is an all-rank structural result, not a finite table or a routine recomputation.
